definition: PerformanceAnalytics is an R package for analyzing financial returns, investment performance and portfolio risk.
example: An analyst plots the drawdown history of a set of monthly returns.

definition: Periscope Data was a business intelligence platform for querying data and sharing dashboards and analyses.
example: An analyst publishes a dashboard driven by SQL queries against a data warehouse.

definition: Periscope was a social video platform for broadcasting live video and interacting with viewers.
example: A presenter streamed a live event and responded to comments during the broadcast.
sense_note: The platform hint suggests the discontinued streaming service; distinguish an optical periscope and Periscope Data.

definition: Permit to work is a formal safety control that authorizes specified work only under documented conditions, responsibilities and precautions.
example: A site supervisor reviews and authorizes a permit before a contractor begins covered work.

definition: Personal Printer Data Stream is an IBM printer command language for describing page content and controlling compatible printers.
example: A legacy application sends PPDS commands to format text on a supported printer.

definition: Personal protective equipment consists of items worn to reduce exposure to hazards that remain after other controls are applied.
example: A worker uses appropriate eye protection during a designated workshop task.

definition: Personalization adapts content, products or interactions to an individual's context, behavior or stated preferences.
example: A news service lets readers prioritize stories from topics they choose.

definition: PEST analysis examines political, economic, social and technological factors in an organization's external environment.
example: A strategy team evaluates how changing consumer habits and new technology could affect a market entry.

definition: Pet insurance sales explain animal insurance products, terms and exclusions and assist customers with purchases under applicable rules.
example: A representative explains waiting periods and coverage limits for a prospective policy.

definition: Phalcon is a PHP web framework implemented in part as a native extension.
example: A developer uses its routing and model components to build a database-backed web application.

definition: PhantomJS was a scriptable headless browser based on WebKit and used for automated page interactions.
example: A team used it to render test pages without a visible browser window.
sense_note: Historical tool; do not imply current support or browser compatibility.

definition: Pharmaceutical batch documentation records the materials, processing steps, checks, deviations and approvals for a specific pharmaceutical production batch.
example: A quality reviewer checks that the reported lot numbers match the approved material records.

definition: Pharmacy operations coordinate the workflow, inventory, staffing and quality controls that support dispensing and related services.
example: A pharmacy manager monitors order queues and verifies that stock records reflect received items.

definition: Photo retouching makes targeted corrections or enhancements to a photograph while maintaining the desired appearance and fidelity.
example: An editor removes scanner dust without altering the image's subject.

definition: phpBB is web forum software for hosting threaded discussions and managing users, categories and moderation.
example: A moderator creates a support category and manages posts reported by members.

definition: phpDesigner is a development environment for writing, editing and debugging PHP and related web code.
example: A developer uses the editor to trace an error in a PHP page.

definition: phpdocx is a PHP library for generating and modifying Microsoft Word documents in DOCX format.
example: A service creates personalized reports from a reusable document template.

definition: PhpED is an integrated development environment for developing and debugging PHP applications.
example: A programmer sets a breakpoint to inspect a variable during local execution.

definition: PHPExcel was a PHP library for reading, writing and manipulating spreadsheet files.
example: A legacy application used PHPExcel to export a workbook with a summary worksheet.
sense_note: Distinguish this historical project from its successor PhpSpreadsheet.

definition: phpFox is software for building online communities and social networking websites.
example: An organization creates a community site with member profiles and groups.

definition: phpGroupWare was a web-based collaboration suite providing shared tools such as calendars and contacts.
example: A team used its shared calendar to coordinate meeting times.

definition: phpLDAPadmin is a web interface for browsing and administering LDAP directories.
example: An administrator reviews directory entries through its browser interface.

definition: phpList is software for managing mailing lists and sending email campaigns to their subscribers.
example: A nonprofit sends a newsletter to an opted-in mailing list.

definition: PHPMailer is a PHP library for composing and sending email, with support for SMTP and multipart messages.
example: A web application sends a receipt email with a plain-text version and a PDF attachment.

definition: phpPgAdmin is a web-based administration tool for PostgreSQL databases.
example: A database administrator inspects the columns and constraints in a test database.

definition: PHPUnit is a PHP testing framework for writing and running automated tests and assertions.
example: A developer tests whether a price calculation rounds correctly for a sample order.

definition: phpWebSite was a content management system for creating and administering websites with modular components.
example: A site editor used it to publish a news article and a calendar entry.

definition: PhpWiki is wiki software written in PHP that allows users to create and collaboratively edit pages.
example: A team maintains a set of linked reference pages for recurring procedures.

definition: Physical modelling synthesis generates sound by simulating the behavior of a sound-producing physical system.
example: A synthesizer models how a plucked string vibrates and loses energy over time.
sense_note: The label is interpreted in its audio-synthesis sense.

definition: Physical vapor deposition applies a thin coating by vaporizing material and depositing it onto a surface in a controlled environment.
example: A manufacturer coats a component with a thin wear-resistant layer.

definition: Piano playing uses keyboard technique, musical interpretation and coordination to perform music on a piano.
example: A pianist balances the loudness of accompaniment and melody while playing a piece.

definition: Pilates is a method of controlled exercise emphasizing coordination, breathing and muscular control.
example: An instructor guides a participant through a controlled movement while cueing breathing.

definition: Pinterest is a visual discovery platform where users find, save and organize images and linked ideas into collections.
example: A designer collects reference images in a project board.

definition: Pipeline pigging sends an internal device through a pipeline to clean, separate materials or inspect its condition.
example: An operator reviews the inspection records from a pig run to plan maintenance.

definition: Pivotal Tracker was an agile project management tool that organized software work into stories, backlogs and iterations.
example: A team used its backlog to prioritize features for a forthcoming iteration.

definition: Pixel art creates digital images by deliberately arranging and coloring individual pixels or small pixel clusters.
example: A game artist creates a character sprite that remains readable at a low resolution.

definition: PixiJS is a JavaScript rendering library for displaying high-performance two-dimensional graphics on the web.
example: A developer uses animated sprites to display a game scene in a web page.

definition: The Plant Design Management System was a three-dimensional computer-aided design system for industrial plant layouts and equipment models.
example: An engineer coordinates piping routes with structural components in a shared plant model.
sense_note: The generic label is interpreted as the product commonly abbreviated PDMS.

definition: Plant design plans the layout, equipment and supporting systems of a facility to meet process, safety and operating requirements.
example: An engineering team positions equipment to allow maintenance access and efficient material flow.
sense_note: The likely sense is industrial facility design, not arranging plants in a landscape.

definition: PlateSpin Migrate is software for transferring server workloads between supported physical, virtual or cloud environments.
example: An administrator migrates an existing server workload to a virtual environment and validates its operation.
